name: Mogadishu
subtitle: Mogadishu, capital of Somalia: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: Mogadishu was a major medieval commercial centre on the East African coast, and the Arab traveller Ibn Battuta described it around 1331 as a large town.
The city became a regional gold-trade centre and seaport handling goods from Africa, India and Arab lands.

parts.text: Mogadishu was a major medieval commercial centre on the East African coast, and the Arab traveller Ibn Battuta described it around 1331 as a large town.
The city became a regional gold-trade centre and seaport handling goods from Africa, India and Arab lands.
After Italian occupation in the late 19th century, Mogadishu became the capital of Italian Somaliland; the former colony became independent in 1960.
A civil war that began in 1991 devastated the city, which has since been in a long process of revitalisation.
Al Jazeera reported on 25 Nov 2025 that the city is bustling but still on guard against al-Shabab.

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in Mogadishu?

parts.text: 1,650,227 in 2014, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Population Estimation Survey 2014 result for Banaadir region (which covers the Mogadishu urban area), tabulated by citypopulation.de for Mogadishu.

items.text: Construction of the Friday mosque at Hamar Weyne began, according to its inscription.
The Arba'a Rukun mosque was built (dated by inscription to ca. 1268-9).
Ibn Battuta visited and called Mogadishu a large town.
Zanzibar's sultan 'ceded' the coastal towns to Italy, a cession described as not really his to make.
The cathedral, modelled on Cefalu in Sicily, was built under Italian colonial rule.
The former colony became independent as the United Republic of Somalia.
Civil war began; the National Museum closed at its start.
The National Museum was reopened after nearly 30 years closed.
